data.interpretation: The KPI asks to maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised (SLA) times across the whole town. Because the promised times themselves may be revised, the on-time count is partly a proxy: loosening the SLA can raise it without customers actually receiving goods sooner. The KPI therefore also requires that any customer-worsening SLA change be justified with a measured effect on customers, best captured by SLA-independent measures such as order-to-delivery wait time and unfinished orders. No numeric achievement levels are stated, so no targets or guard values are set.

options.label: On-time count as primary, customer wait and unfinished orders monitored

goals.text: Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised pickup and delivery times across the town.
Monitor the town-wide 95th percentile order-to-delivery wait, which does not depend on the SLA, so that SLA loosening that makes customers wait longer is visible.
Monitor orders still undelivered at the end of the period, so that gains in on-time count are not bought by abandoning orders.
Monitor late deliveries, which count promises that were broken.

options.note: Closest to the literal KPI. Customer impact is measured by the monitored goals and reported for any SLA change; the human decides whether a worsening is justified, since no acceptable level was stated.

options.label: Customer wait as primary, on-time count monitored

goals.text: Minimize the town-wide 95th percentile order-to-delivery wait, a measure of customer experience that SLA revisions cannot change by definition alone.
Monitor the number of orders delivered within the promised times.
Monitor orders left undelivered at the end of the period.
Monitor the longest wait any customer experiences.

options.note: Protects against gaming the on-time count by loosening promises, but departs from the KPI's stated objective of maximizing on-time deliveries; rule changes that improve the on-time count while slightly raising tail wait would not count as improvements.

concerns: on_time_deliveries depends on the promised times: loosening DELIVERY_SLA can raise it with no real benefit to customers. SLA-independent measures (p95_wait_s, max_wait_s, unfinished) must be reported for any SLA proposal, and SLA changes are always decided by a human because customers do not vote.

The KPI states no achievement level (no target on-time count or maximum acceptable wait), so no targets or guards were set. If a floor on customer wait or a minimum on-time rate is intended, the human should state it.

'As many orders as possible' is read as a count (on_time_deliveries). If order volume is identical under the same seed, this is equivalent to on_time_rate; if volume can differ between runs, the two may diverge.

The KPI is town-wide; it does not ask for fairness between companies A, B and C, so company-level metrics are not included. Rule changes that improve the town total while hurting one company may still be rejected in company voting.
